speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the nature of the pain in your right knee and how long the swelling has been present? Also, have you noticed any redness or warmth in the joint? Finally, do you recall any recent infections, such as a sore throat or skin infection, before these symptoms started?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any discharge from your penis, or have you noticed a rash on your skin or redness in your eyes? Given your sexual history and symptoms, I need to rule out a specific infection. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Urine Culture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Protein Negative, Blood Negative, WBC 12–16/hpf, RBC 1–2/hpf. Urine Culture: Not performed in available data. Note: ELISA for HIV is Negative.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any current penile discharge, and have you noticed any eye redness or skin rashes since the ankle pain started? Given the combination of joint pain, urinary symptoms, and sexual history, I need to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Nucleic Acid Amplification Test (NAAT) for Chlamydia and Gonorrhea.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Nucleic Acid Amplification Test (NAAT) for Chlamydia and Gonorrhea: Not performed in available data. Note: Urinalysis shows WBC 12–16/hpf; ELISA for HIV is Negative; Arthrocentesis of Right Knee shows 26,000/mm3 leukocytes with 75% neutrophils and cloudy appearance.

speaker: Doctor
text: The arthrocentesis results showing cloudy fluid with high neutrophil counts, combined with your urinary symptoms and recent joint involvement, strongly suggest reactive arthritis triggered by an STI. Do you recall any redness in your eyes or a rash on your palms or soles since these symptoms began?

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your anxious appearance and the specific combination of urethritis, asymmetric arthritis, and the high neutrophil count in your knee fluid, do you have any redness in your eyes or a rash on your hands or feet to complete the classic triad? REQUEST TEST: HLA-B27 Antigen.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Not performed in available data. Note: Ophthalmologic examination confirms bilateral inflammation of the conjunctiva; Arthrocentesis of Right Knee shows cloudy fluid with 26,000/mm3 leukocytes (75% neutrophils); ELISA for HIV is Negative; Urinalysis shows WBC 12–16/hpf.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of urethritis, asymmetric arthritis, and confirmed conjunctivitis completes the classic triad for Reactive Arthritis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis
